quote: sanctions are unavailable unless served before the case is disposed of
text: Sanctions are unavailable unless the motion is served before the case is disposed of. As the court put it, "sanctions are unavailable unless served before the case is disposed of" Ridder v. City of Springfield, 109 F.3d 288.
decision: Ifeoma Delliane Chinedu Obi v. Cook County, Illinois, et al. (1)
court_finding: Plaintiff quoted Ridder v. City of Springfield (109 F.3d 288) as saying sanctions are unavailable unless served before the case is disposed of; Court found that language is not in Ridder.

name: Garrett v. Selby Connor Maddux & Janer
text: Opposing counsel may prey on the ignorance of pro se litigants. See Garrett v. Selby Connor Maddux & Janer, 425 F.3d 836.
decision: Kevin Lee Biglow v. Dell Technologies Inc.
court_finding: Attributed a quote about opposing counsel preying on pro se ignorance to Garrett v. Selby Connor Maddux & Janer, 425 F.3d 836, 840; the court found no such language in Garrett.

name: Duff v. Trenton Beverage Co.
text: A contract never becomes binding if a condition precedent is not completed. As the court put it, "never becomes binding" Duff v. Trenton Beverage Co., 73 A.2d 578.
decision: Lawand Hill v. Sloppy Vinyl, LLC, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Duff v. Trenton Beverage Co., 73 A.2d 578 (1950) for the proposition that a contract 'never becomes binding' if a condition precedent is not completed; the court found the quoted language does not appear in Duff.

name: Jordan v. Fox, Rothschild, O’Brien & Frankel
quote: may not consider matters extraneous to the pleadings
text: A district court may not consider matters extraneous to the pleadings on a motion to dismiss. As the court put it, "may not consider matters extraneous to the pleadings" Jordan v. Fox, Rothschild, O’Brien & Frankel, 20 F.3d 1250.
decision: Lawand Hill v. Sloppy Vinyl, LLC, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Jordan v. Fox, Rothschild, O’Brien & Frankel, 20 F.3d 1250 (3d Cir. 1994) for the proposition that a district court 'may not consider matters extraneous to the pleadings' on a motion to dismiss; the court found that quoted language does not appear in Jordan.

name: United States v. Jackson
text: Informing authorities of misconduct cannot constitute an unlawful threat. See United States v. Jackson, 180 F.3d 55.
decision: Kettering Adventist Healthcare v. Sandra Collier, et al.
court_finding: Counsel quoted or paraphrased United States v. Jackson, 180 F.3d 55 (2d Cir. 1999) as saying that informing authorities of misconduct cannot be an unlawful threat; the Court found no such language in Jackson and that the opinion does not stand for the asserted proposition.

name: Raymond F. v. Dep't of Econ. Sec.
quote: [a] parent who creates barriers to contact through substance abuse cannot claim just cause for his failure to maintain a relationship.
text: A parent who creates barriers to contact through substance abuse cannot claim just cause for his failure to maintain a relationship with the child. As the court put it, "[a] parent who creates barriers to contact through substance abuse cannot claim just cause for his failure to maintain a relationship." Raymond F. v. Dep't of Econ. Sec., 224 Ariz. 373.
decision: In re termination of parental rights (HK)
court_finding: Mother's brief attributed a non-existent quote to Raymond F. v. Dep't of Econ. Sec., 224 Ariz. 373, 378, ¶ 21 (App. 2010): '[a] parent who creates barriers to contact through substance abuse cannot claim just cause for his failure to maintain a relationship.' The court found this quotation does not appear in Raymond F.

name: EEOC v. Great Steaks, Inc.
quote: fees for defendants appropriate only in "egregious cases"
text: Attorney's fees may be awarded to defendants only in egregious cases. As the court put it, "fees for defendants appropriate only in 'egregious cases'" EEOC v. Great Steaks, Inc., 667 F.3d 510.
decision: Taylor v. Prince George’s County, Maryland
court_finding: Plaintiffs quoted language attributed to EEOC v. Great Steaks, Inc., 667 F.3d 510, 516 (4th Cir. 2012) (e.g., 'fees for defendants appropriate only in "egregious cases"'), but the opinion does not contain the quoted language.

name: Taylor v. Brighton Corp.
quote: OSHA does not create a private cause of action
text: OSHA does not create a private cause of action. As the court put it, "OSHA does not create a private cause of action" Taylor v. Brighton Corp., 616 F.2d 256.
decision: Thomas Duncan v. Gridhawk et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Taylor v. Brighton Corp., 616 F.2d 256, 258 (5th Cir. 1980) and attributed the quotation 'OSHA does not create a private cause of action' to it; the court found the case exists but does not contain that quoted language (false quote).

name: Jones v. Buchanan
text: A minimal level of force can violate a prisoner's constitutional rights. As the court put it, "a minimal level of force" Jones v. Buchanan, 325 F.3d 520.
decision: Neal v. Frayer
court_finding: Counsel placed a parenthetical quote attributed to Jones v. Buchanan, 325 F.3d 520 (4th Cir. 2003) ('a minimal level of force' can violate rights) that does not appear in the opinion; the opinion instead involved substantial force.

name: United States v. Edwards
quote: packaging weight should not be included
text: Packaging weight should not be included in calculating the drug quantity for sentencing. As the court put it, "packaging weight should not be included" United States v. Edwards, 188 F.3d 230.
decision: United States of America v. Lorenzio Reshaud Simmons
court_finding: Memorandum cited 'United States v. Edwards, 188 F.3d 230, 232 (4th Cir. 1999)' and quoted that packaging weight should not be included; court found Edwards does not contain that quoted language (false quotation).

name: Crescent Towing & Salvage Co. v. M/V ANAX
quote: [T]he maritime lien includes the principal debt, interest and reasonable attorney's fees, where provided for in the contract.
text: The maritime lien includes the principal debt, interest, and reasonable attorney's fees, where provided for in the contract. As the court put it, "[T]he maritime lien includes the principal debt, interest and reasonable attorney's fees, where provided for in the contract." Crescent Towing & Salvage Co. v. M/V ANAX, 40 F.3d 741.
decision: Pennantia v. Rose Cay Maritime
court_finding: Brief attributed: '[T]he maritime lien includes the principal debt, interest and reasonable attorney's fees, where provided for in the contract.' to Crescent Towing & Salvage Co. v. M/V ANAX (40 F.3d 741, 744 (5th Cir. 1994)); court found the quoted language absent from that opinion and not located elsewhere.

name: General Elec. Credit Corp. v. Drill Ship Mission Exploration
quote: The term "necessaries" includes the contract price, including interest if agreed or customary.
text: The term 'necessaries' includes the contract price, including interest if agreed or customary. As the court put it, "The term 'necessaries' includes the contract price, including interest if agreed or customary." General Elec. Credit Corp. v. Drill Ship Mission Exploration, 668 F.2d 811.
decision: Pennantia v. Rose Cay Maritime
court_finding: Brief attributed: 'The term "necessaries" includes the contract price, including interest if agreed or customary.' to General Elec. Credit Corp. v. Drill Ship Mission Exploration (668 F.2d 811, 815 (5th Cir. 1982)); court found the quoted language absent from that opinion and not located elsewhere.

name: Doe v. F.B.I.
quote: Parties may not evade service by hiding behind pseudonyms while continuing to engage in legal actions using those same identities.
text: Parties may not evade service by hiding behind pseudonyms while continuing to engage in legal actions using those same identities. As the court put it, "Parties may not evade service by hiding behind pseudonyms while continuing to engage in legal actions using those same identities." Doe v. F.B.I., 218 F.R.D. 256.
decision: Evans, et al. v. Robertson et al. (2)
court_finding: Evans attributed the quotation “Parties may not evade service by hiding behind pseudonyms while continuing to engage in legal actions using those same identities.” to Doe v. F.B.I., 218 F.R.D. 256 (D. Colo. 2003); court found no such language in that case or elsewhere.

name: Union Planters v. L&J Dev. Co.
text: Rule 11 sanctions are reserved for exceptional circumstances. As the court put it, "reserved for exceptional circumstances" Union Planters v. L&J Dev. Co., 115 F.3d 378.
decision: Ali v. IT People Corporation
court_finding: Plaintiff falsely represented that Union Planters v. L&J Dev. Co., 115 F.3d 378 (6th Cir. 1997) contained language holding that Rule 11 sanctions are “reserved for exceptional circumstances”; court found this a false quotation and pivotal misrepresentation.

name: Universal City Dev. Partners, Ltd. v. Ride & Show
quote: is tantamount to no objection at all.
text: A response that fails to make a specific objection is tantamount to no objection at all. As the court put it, "is tantamount to no objection at all." Universal City Dev. Partners, Ltd. v. Ride & Show, 230 F.R.D. 688.
decision: Crespo v. Tesla, Inc.
court_finding: Plaintiff quoted Universal City Dev. Partners, Ltd. v. Ride & Show, 230 F.R.D. 688, 695 (M.D. Fla. 2005) as saying “is tantamount to no objection at all.” (DE 78 at 2); the Court found no such quote exists in that case.

name: University of Tennessee v. Elliott
text: All doubts must be resolved in favor of remand. See University of Tennessee v. Elliott, 478 U.S. 788.
decision: Thornton v. Amazon.com Services LLC
court_finding: Plaintiff cited University of Tennessee v. Elliott, 478 U.S. 788, 799, for the statement that all doubts must be resolved in favor of remand. The court found that the case contains neither the quotation nor discussion of removal.

name: Ackerman v. Upper Mt. Bethel Township
text: The Sunshine Act applies to the agency and to each participating member. See Ackerman v. Upper Mt. Bethel Township, 567 A.2d 1116.
decision: Coyne v. Smurl
court_finding: The plaintiffs cited “Ackerman v. Upper Mt. Bethel Township, Commonwealth Court, 2015” and claimed it held that the Sunshine Act applies to the agency and each participating member. The court found no such 2015 decision, identified the actual case as Ackerman v. Upper Mt. Bethel Township, 567 A.2d 1116 (Pa. Cmwlth. 1989), and stated that it did not contain the quoted proposition.

name: Goodman v. Illinois Dep't of Financial & Professional Regulation
text: The ADA does not provide compensatory or punitive damages. See Goodman v. Illinois Dep't of Financial & Professional Regulation, 430 F.3d 432.
decision: Morgan Cole v. Hobby Town Unlimited, Inc.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Goodman v. Illinois Dep't of Financial & Professional Regulation, 430 F.3d 432 (7th Cir. 2005) as authority that the ADA does not provide compensatory or punitive damages, but Goodman concerns a First Amendment challenge and does not address the ADA.

name: Sierra Club v. Franklin County Power of Illinois, LLC
text: Required fixes are modest in cost. See Sierra Club v. Franklin County Power of Illinois, LLC, 546 F.3d 918.
decision: Morgan Cole v. Hobby Town Unlimited, Inc.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Sierra Club v. Franklin County Power of Illinois, LLC, 546 F.3d 918 (7th Cir. 2008) to support that required fixes are modest in cost, but Sierra Club addresses environmental injunctive relief and is unrelated to website accessibility costs.

name: Traguth v. Zuck
text: Courts must afford special solicitude to pro se prisoner litigants in construing their pleadings. See Traguth v. Zuck, 710 F.2d 90.
decision: Nirav Modi v. Richard Levin, Trustee for the Liquidating Trust of Firestar Diamond, Inc.
court_finding: Citation to Traguth v. Zuck, 710 F.2d 90 (2d Cir. 1983) invoked to support special solicitude to pro se prisoners, but the cited opinion's facts and holdings do not support that proposition as presented.

name: Avery v. State Farm
text: Consumer Fraud Act damages claims are legal claims triable to a jury. See Avery v. State Farm, 216 Ill. 2d 100.
decision: Cole v. Lee
court_finding: Cited Avery v. State Farm, 216 Ill. 2d 100 (2005) for the proposition that Consumer Fraud Act damages claims are legal claims triable to a jury; court found Avery contains no support for that proposition.

name: People ex rel. Daley v. Datacom Systems Corp.
text: Where legal and equitable issues are joined, the legal issues must be tried to a jury. See People ex rel. Daley v. Datacom Systems Corp., 146 Ill. 2d 1.
decision: Cole v. Lee
court_finding: Cited People ex rel. Daley v. Datacom Systems Corp., 146 Ill. 2d 1 (1991) as supporting that joined legal and equitable issues require the legal issues be tried to a jury; court found Datacom contains no support for that proposition.

name: Pierce v. Cnty. of Orange
text: The continuing-violation doctrine applies to extend the statute of limitations for the plaintiff's claims because the discriminatory conduct continued into the limitations period. See Pierce v. Cnty. of Orange, 526 F.3d 1190.
decision: Kimberly A. Graves v. Pacific Gas and Electric Company
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on Pierce v. Cnty. of Orange, 526 F.3d 1190 (9th Cir. 2008) for a statute-of-limitations/continuing-violation proposition; court noted the cited opinion exists but does not discuss the statute-of-limitations or continuing-violation issues relied upon, i.e., a mischaracterization of precedent.

name: Gutierrez v. Kermon
text: De minimis injuries do not rise to the level of a constitutional violation. See Gutierrez v. Kermon, 722 F.3d 1003.
decision: John P. Chapman v. Officer Decker et al.
court_finding: Defendants cited Gutierrez v. Kermon, 722 F.3d 1003, 1011 (7th Cir. 2013) for the proposition that de minimis injuries do not rise to a constitutional violation; the Court found Gutierrez did not address that proposition as cited.

name: Gene & Gene LLC v. BioPay LLC
text: The §227(c)(5) safe-harbor applies only where the defendant actually complied with the procedures required to avoid liability for telephone solicitation violations. See Gene & Gene LLC v. BioPay LLC, 541 F.3d 318.
decision: McCormick v. Texakoma Financial
court_finding: Citation to Gene & Gene LLC v. BioPay LLC, 541 F.3d 318 (5th Cir. 2008) was used to support a proposition about the §227(c)(5) safe-harbor requiring actual compliance, but the cited pages do not support that proposition.

name: Shields Ltd. P'ship v. Bradberry
text: A party has a duty to speak and may be estopped from asserting a position when its silence would mislead another party relying on that silence. See Shields Ltd. P'ship v. Bradberry, 526 S.W.3d 471.
decision: McCormick v. Texakoma Financial
court_finding: Citation to Shields Ltd. P'ship v. Bradberry, 526 S.W.3d 471 (Tex. 2017) was used to assert a duty-to-speak estoppel principle that the Court found the cited pages do not establish.

name: Hoover v. Langston Equip. Assocs., Inc.
text: No authority imposes fiduciary duties on a client toward his or her lawyer. See Hoover v. Langston Equip. Assocs., Inc., 958 F.2d 742.
decision: Reaves Law Firm, PLLC v. Baker, Donelson, Bearman, Caldwell & Berkowitz, PC, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Hoover v. Langston Equip. Assocs., Inc., 958 F.2d 742 (6th Cir. 1992) as supporting that no authority imposes fiduciary duties from a client to a lawyer; court noted Hoover did not address attorney-client fiduciary duty and was misapplied.

name: S.M. v. J.M.
text: Failing to remedy parental alienation would irreparably harm the child. As the court put it, "irreparably harm" S.M. v. J.M., 811 A.2d 621.
decision: Jaclyn Cocco v. Rosario Palmieri, Jr.
court_finding: Appellant cited S.M. v. J.M., 811 A.2d 621, 625 (Pa. Super. 2002) as supporting that failing to remedy alienation would 'irreparably harm' the child; the court found the cited opinion does not contain that language nor discuss parental alienation as claimed.

name: Discover Bank v. Stucka
text: Parental alienation is a recognized basis for modifying custody arrangements. See Discover Bank v. Stucka, 33 A.3d 82.
decision: Jaclyn Cocco v. Rosario Palmieri, Jr.
court_finding: Appellant's citation led to Discover Bank v. Stucka, 33 A.3d 82 (Pa. Super. 2011), an opinion unrelated to child custody, which Appellant had relied on for a parental-alienation proposition.

name: Cook v. Randolph Cty.
text: A plaintiff is entitled to amend the complaint under Rule 15 to add new claims. See Cook v. Randolph Cty., 573 F.3d 1143.
decision: Bridgett Watson Adams, et al. v. 3M Company
court_finding: Plaintiffs relied on Cook v. Randolph Cty., 573 F.3d 1143, 1150-51 (11th Cir. 2009) to support a Rule 15 amendment entitlement, but Cook concerned remand and summary judgment—not Rule 15 amendment standards; the case was misread/misapplied.

name: Payton v. Monsanto
text: Under Alabama law, the statute of limitations for the claim accrues under a discovery rule, so it begins to run only when the plaintiff knew or should have known of the injury. See Payton v. Monsanto, 801 So. 2d 829.
decision: Bridgett Watson Adams, et al. v. 3M Company
court_finding: Plaintiffs cited Payton v. Monsanto, 801 So. 2d 829, 835-36 (Ala. 2001) claiming it supported a discovery rule for accrual; the court noted Payton actually rejects such a discovery rule—Plaintiffs mischaracterized the holding.

name: Larson v. Domestic & Foreign Commerce Corp.
text: Courts may void or enjoin public spending that is ultra vires. See Larson v. Domestic & Foreign Commerce Corp., 337 U.S. 682.
decision: Shaw v. City of Portola, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on Larson v. Domestic & Foreign Commerce Corp., 337 U.S. 682 (1949) to support the proposition that courts void or enjoin ultra vires public spending; court found Larson only mentions ultra vires and does not support that spending‑enjoining proposition.

name: Harris v. One Hope United, Inc.
text: Parent and subsidiary corporations may be treated as a single entity. See Harris v. One Hope United, Inc., 28 N.E.3d 804.
decision: Ella and Ramin LLC v. Travelers Insurance Company
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Harris v. One Hope United, Inc., 28 N.E.3d 804 (Ill. 2015) for the proposition that parent and subsidiary may be treated as a single entity, but the case concerns discovery privilege and does not support that corporate-law proposition (misapplied precedent).

name: People v. Panah
quote: Admitting a transcript without the original recording is reversible error.
text: Admitting a transcript without the original recording is reversible error. As the court put it, "Admitting a transcript without the original recording is reversible error." People v. Panah, 35 Cal. 4th 395.
decision: Samuel K. v. Winsley Focia
court_finding: Brief quoted 'Admitting a transcript without the original recording is reversible error.' and cited People v. Panah (2005) 35 Cal.4th 395, 475; court found the quotation does not exist and Panah reached the opposite conclusion.

name: Caruso v. Local Union 690
text: Statements that are defamatory per se are actionable without proof of special damages. See Caruso v. Local Union 690, 107 Wash. 2d 524.
decision: Merz v. City of Kalama
court_finding: Merz relied on Caruso v. Local Union 690, 107 Wn.2d 524, 529-30 (1987) to support a 'per se' defamation assertion; court found the citation misleading because the cited pages do not contain the 'per se' language Merz attributed to it.

name: LeBeau v. Taco Bell, Inc.
text: The two-dismissal rule bars a plaintiff from refiling a voluntarily dismissed action after a second dismissal of the same claims. See LeBeau v. Taco Bell, Inc., 892 F.2d 605.
decision: Bettis v. Gaston
court_finding: Plaintiff cited LeBeau v. Taco Bell, Inc., 892 F.2d 605 (7th Cir. 1989) as supporting the two-dismissal rule, but the court found the opinion does not discuss that rule (misrepresented precedent).

name: Great Earth Companies, Inc. v. Simons
text: Discovery is required to determine whether a dispute is arbitrable. See Great Earth Companies, Inc. v. Simons, 288 F.3d 878.
decision: Rachel Jones v. Experian Information Solutions
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Great Earth Companies, Inc. v. Simons, 288 F.3d 878, 889 (6th Cir. 2002) as supporting the proposition that discovery is required to determine arbitrability; the Court found Great Earth does not address discovery and flagged the misstatement as possibly AI-related.

name: United States v. Helena
text: Only a court, and not a probation officer, may impose conditions of supervised release. See United States v. Helena, 906 F.3d 288.
decision: United States v. Brian Boehm
court_finding: Cited United States v. Helena, 906 F.3d 288, 291 (3d Cir. 2018) to suggest only a court (not probation) may impose supervised-release conditions; Helena did not involve a probation officer imposing conditions and was mischaracterized.

name: Bevill v. Fletcher
text: A judge's pretrial declaration of a defendant's guilt removes judicial immunity and supports a § 1983 retaliation claim. See Bevill v. Fletcher, 26 F.4th 270.
decision: Brick v. Gallatin County, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on Bevill v. Fletcher (26 F.4th 270) as supporting that a judge's pretrial declaration of guilt removes judicial immunity or supports a §1983 retaliation claim; the Court found Plaintiff mischaracterized the actual holdings.

name: People ex rel. State Bd. of Equalization v. Hively
text: Declaratory relief is available to clarify ownership where the parties' rights in the property remain uncertain. See People ex rel. State Bd. of Equalization v. Hively, 336 P.2d 721.
decision: Hanson v. Nest Home Lending, LLC et al.
court_finding: Motion cites People ex rel. State Bd. of Equalization v. Hively, 336 P.2d 721 (1959) for a proposition about declaratory relief and ownership clarity that the case does not establish.

name: Koon v. Barmettler
text: Declaratory judgment is appropriate to resolve a quiet title dispute. See Koon v. Barmettler, 301 P.2d 713.
decision: Hanson v. Nest Home Lending, LLC et al.
court_finding: Motion for Declaratory Judgment cites Koon v. Barmettler, 301 P.2d 713 (1956) for the proposition that declaratory judgment is appropriate to resolve quiet title, but Koon did not address that subject.

name: Strike 3 Holdings, LLC v. Doe
text: Courts approve delayed notice to prevent subpoena targets from learning of the subpoena. See Strike 3 Holdings, LLC v. Doe, 964 F.3d 1203.
decision: Y.S. v. John Doe et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on Strike 3 Holdings, LLC v. Doe, 964 F.3d 1203 (D.C. Cir. 2020) as approving 'delayed notice' to prevent targets from knowing of subpoenas; the court observed Strike 3 contains no discussion of preventing a subpoena target from learning of the subpoena and therefore does not support plaintiff's proposition.

name: Adams v. Rice
text: Collateral estoppel bars relitigation of issues actually decided in an earlier proceeding. See Adams v. Rice, 40 F.3d 72.
decision: Neal v. Frayer
court_finding: Counsel cited Adams v. Rice, 40 F.3d 72 (4th Cir. 1994) as supporting a collateral estoppel point though the opinion addresses IFP dismissal under §1915 and does not discuss collateral estoppel.

name: United States v. Mississippi
text: Disability-based sanctions and adverse inferences are irreversible. See United States v. Mississippi, 82 F.4th 387.
decision: Lareina A. Sauls v. Pierce County, et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on United States v. Mississippi, 82 F.4th 387 (5th Cir. 2023) as supporting the proposition that disability-based sanctions/adverse inferences are irreversible; the Court stated that the cited case does not discuss or support that inference.

name: Scanlan v. Tate Supply, Inc.
text: Due diligence in service of process is a jury question. See Scanlan v. Tate Supply, Inc., 303 Ga. App. 9.
decision: In re: Loletha Hale, Esq. (Boston v. Williams)
court_finding: Cited Scanlan v. Tate Supply, Inc., 303 Ga. App. 9 (2010) as holding due diligence in service is a jury question; court found Scanlan holds the opposite (diligence is for the trial court).

name: Akuoko v. Martin
text: Due diligence is a question for the jury. See Akuoko v. Martin, 298 Ga. App. 364.
decision: In re: Loletha Hale, Esq. (Boston v. Williams)
court_finding: Cited Akuoko v. Martin, 298 Ga. App. 364 (2009) as supporting that due diligence is a jury question; court noted Akuoko actually treats diligence as a question for the trial court.

name: United States v. Brehm
quote: any uncertainty should be resolved in the defendant's favor.
text: Any uncertainty should be resolved in the defendant's favor. As the court put it, "any uncertainty should be resolved in the defendant's favor." United States v. Brehm, 442 F.3d 1291.
decision: United States of America v. Lorenzio Reshaud Simmons
court_finding: Memorandum cited 'United States v. Brehm, 442 F.3d 1291, 1293 (4th Cir. 2006)' and attributed the quote 'any uncertainty should be resolved in the defendant's favor.' The court noted the cited Brehm reference is to a different circuit and does not contain that quoted language.

name: United States v. Harrision
text: Laboratory testing is more precise than other methods of identification. See United States v. Harrision, 918 F.2d 469.
decision: United States of America v. Lorenzio Reshaud Simmons
court_finding: Memorandum cited 'United States v. Harrision, 918 F.2d 469, 473 (4th Cir. 1990)' for a statement that laboratory testing is more precise; court noted the correct case is in a different circuit (Fifth) and does not contain that quoted text.

name: Semitool, Inc. v. Tokyo Electron Am., Inc.
text: Good cause for a protective order or discovery relief requires consideration of a specific four-factor test. See Semitool, Inc. v. Tokyo Electron Am., Inc., 208 F.R.D. 273.
decision: Jade Riley Burch v. HCA Healthcare
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Semitool, Inc. v. Tokyo Electron Am., Inc., 208 F.R.D. 273 (N.D. Cal. 2002); the citation is real but the plaintiff attributed a specific four-factor 'good cause' formulation to it that the court says the case does not actually announce.

name: Peake v. Underwood
text: Sanctions are warranted when a party files a second dispositive motion. See Peake v. Underwood, 227 Cal. App. 4th 428.
decision: Noland v. Land
court_finding: Appellant cited Peake v. Underwood (227 Cal.App.4th 428) as supporting sanctions for filing a second dispositive motion, but the court does not address that issue; the citation was misused/false.

name: Fujita v. United States
text: The Fifth Circuit affirmed the denial of a stay. See Fujita v. United States, 416 F. App'x 400.
decision: Blake Lewis v. Entergy Mississippi, LLC
court_finding: Counsel cited Fujita v. United States, 416 F. App'x 400, 402 (5th Cir. 2011) as affirming denial of a stay; the Court found the Fujita opinion actually affirmed the district court's grant of a stay and stated the stay was proper.

name: Penthouse Int'l, Ltd. v. Playboy Enters., Inc.
text: Under the doctrine of estoppel and apparent authority, a principal is bound by the acts of an agent when the principal's conduct leads a third party reasonably to believe the agent has authority to act. See Penthouse Int'l, Ltd. v. Playboy Enters., Inc., 663 F.2d 371.
decision: Hocog v. Cook-Huynh
court_finding: Cited Penthouse Int'l, Ltd. v. Playboy Enters., Inc. (663 F.2d 371 (2d Cir. 1981)) for an estoppel/apparent authority principle that the court found is not discussed in that opinion.

name: Landale Enters. v. Berry
text: Third-party disclaimers are defeated where the disclaiming party's rights are not otherwise preserved. See Landale Enters. v. Berry, 676 F.2d 506.
decision: Axis Dynamics, Inc. v. Knox County, Tennessee
court_finding: Plaintiffs cited Landale Enters. v. Berry, 676 F.2d 506 (11th Cir. 1982) as supporting the defeat of third-party disclaimers; the court found Landale does not address third-party rights disclaimers and does not support Plaintiffs' proposition.

name: Brown v. Gadsden Regional Medical Center, LLC
text: A direct payment made to a provider creates a beneficiary relationship with the payor, even where the contract contains a disclaimer. See Brown v. Gadsden Regional Medical Center, LLC, 748 F. App'x 930.
decision: Axis Dynamics, Inc. v. Knox County, Tennessee
court_finding: Plaintiffs cited Brown v. Gadsden Regional Medical Center, LLC, 748 Fed. App'x 930 (11th Cir. 2018) as supporting a direct-payment-created beneficiary; the court found Brown actually held the opposite given a disclaimer in the contract.

name: Sheriff v. Marcum
text: Threats render an agreement void rather than merely voidable. See Sheriff v. Marcum, 105 Nev. 824.
decision: Angela Williams, et al. v. Jamal Rashid, et al.
court_finding: Briefs cite Sheriff v. Marcum, 105 Nev. 824, 828 (1989) for the proposition that threats render agreements void rather than voidable; court found Marcum exists but is a habeas case that does not address that proposition (misrepresented precedent).

name: Kirkland v. American Title Ins. Co.
text: Service of process by certified mail is valid and sufficient under the circumstances presented. See Kirkland v. American Title Ins. Co., 692 F. Supp. 153.
decision: Graciela Dela Torre v. Davies Life & Health, Inc., et al.
court_finding: Plaintiff cited Kirkland v. American Title Ins. Co., '692 F. Supp. 153, 155 (N.D. Ill. 1988)' to support certified-mail service; the court found the opinion was from the Eastern District of New York and contains no discussion of certified mail, so the citation was misapplied/misrepresented.

name: Trotter v. Jack Anderson Enterprises, Inc.
text: Calling someone 'aggressive' carries a defamatory sting. See Trotter v. Jack Anderson Enterprises, Inc., 818 F.2d 431.
decision: Buckner v. Hilton Global
court_finding: Plaintiff relied on Trotter v. Jack Anderson Enterprises, Inc., 818 F.2d 431 (5th Cir. 1987) as supporting that calling someone 'aggressive' carries defamatory sting; the Court found Trotter did not discuss that proposition.

name: E.E.C. v. E.J.C.
text: Harm to a business flows to its owner, so the owner has standing to sue for injuries suffered by the business. See E.E.C. v. E.J.C., 457 A.2d 688.
decision: Mark Lillard v. Offit Kurman, P.A.
